body: This project is quite good, but the text scrolling isn't smooth—it jumps in blocks instead of moving continuously. It feels quite jarring and I hope it can be improved for a more seamless experience.

comments.body:
Hi @KingingWang! 

Could you describe the issue a bit more? Are you experiencing this on web or on mobile via remote access from a browser?
If its remote access from mobile web browser, 100% know that experience is not the cleanest. working on a nicer solution for that - but in the meantime for smoother scrollability and easier review of terminal output and being able to copy/paste/etc - use the "read" option on the bottom left. it puts the terminal in a read mode thats a much smoother experience (to exit out click the x button on the top right).

Let me know if that helps or if the issue described is different!

Thanks for the feedback @KingingWang!

The "block scrolling" you're seeing is an inherent behavior of xterm.js, the terminal emulator library. It renders via HTML canvas in discrete row increments rather than smooth pixel scrolling. This is the same behavior you'd see in native terminals like Windows Terminal or iTerm2 when scrolling through output.

A few things that may help:
- **Keyboard scrolling** (Shift+Up/Down or Shift+PageUp/PageDown) gives line-by-line control
- **Mouse wheel scrolling** moves in 3-line increments (standard terminal behavior)
- If you're seeing particularly large "jumps" in the active pane, that could indicate a rendering issue. Could you share which browser and OS you're on?

Smooth pixel-by-pixel scrolling would require changes upstream in xterm.js itself. Keeping this open to track interest, but it's not something we can address at the Myrlin level.

title: The sliding experience is not good

body:
Not sure how feasible it is, CC doesn't use a server/client structure...

Sharing Opus's Thought on this
```
 Good question — this is architecturally interesting. Let me give you an honest breakdown of what's technically feasible.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  The Core Problem                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  A running Claude Code process has a PTY pair:                                                           
  - slave end — held by claude (what it reads/writes)
  - master end — held by whatever terminal started it (Terminal.app, iTerm2, etc.)

  Myrlin only controls PTYs it spawns — it has no handle to the master end of someone else's PTY.

  ---
  What's Actually Possible

  1. /dev/tty device sharing — works on macOS, best native option

  Every terminal process has a TTY device like /dev/ttys003. Since it's the same user, you can open it:

  ps -p <pid> -o tty=          # → s003
  # /dev/ttys003 is readable/writable by the owning user

  Implementation in Myrlin:
  1. Scan ps output for claude processes with --resume <uuid> or that have the session's JSONL file open (lsof)
  2. Get their TTY via ps -o tty=
  3. Open /dev/ttys003 as a raw fd in node-pty or a raw stream
  4. Pipe it into the WebSocket like any other PTY

  Downside: you're sharing the same PTY master, so both the original terminal and Myrlin's WebSocket client are receiving and sending input simultaneously — it gets messy unless you're careful (read-only
  mirror vs. full control).

  ---
  2. tmux integration — cleanest UX, requires tmux

  If the user runs Claude inside tmux (common), Myrlin can detect which pane holds the session and use tmux's built-in multiplexing:

  # Find pane running claude with session uuid
  tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command} #{pane_pid}'

  # "Attach" by piping through tmux's pipe-pane or just connecting another client:
  tmux attach-session -t <session>:<window>.<pane>

  This is genuinely shared — multiple views of the exact same running process.

  ---
  3. Long-term clean solution — Myrlin owns the PTY from birth

  For sessions started from Myrlin, this is already solved — Myrlin holds the master PTY. The discovered sessions problem only exists for sessions started externally. The real fix is: make it easy enough to
  launch from Myrlin that users stop launching externally.

  ---
  What I'd Recommend

  The /dev/tty approach (#1) is self-contained (no tmux dependency) and would work today. The implementation would be a new branch in attachClient:

  if (session is a discovered live process) {
    find PID by scanning ps for claude --resume <uuid>
    get TTY device from ps -o tty
    open /dev/ttys<N> as a readable stream
    pipe to WebSocket (read-only mirror, or full bidirectional)
  } else {
    current spawn path
  }

  Want me to prototype this? The main challenges to sort out first:
  - PID lookup: reliable way to match a Claude session UUID to a running PID
  - Read-only vs full control: do you want the Myrlin view to be a passive mirror, or should it be able to send input too (which the original terminal also sees)?
  - 
 ```

comments.body:
Hey AX! Great writeup and thanks for having Opus think through this -- the /dev/tty approach is interesting.

You're right that the core tension is: Myrlin only controls PTYs it spawns. For discovered sessions, we're reading JSONL data (conversation history, cost, subagent tracking) but not attaching to the live terminal.

I think the pragmatic path forward is option 3 (make it easy to launch from Myrlin) which is where we're headed -- the worktree task system, templates, and project context launch already make Myrlin the natural starting point. The fewer externally-started sessions, the less this matters.

That said, a read-only mirror via /dev/tty would be a cool power-user feature down the line. The main concern would be macOS vs Linux TTY device differences and making sure we don't accidentally inject input into someone's running session.

Going to label this as a future enhancement -- appreciate you opening it!

Thank you for considering! Really enjoyed Myrlin :)

Thanks for the detailed writeup @xingfanxia, and for including Opus's architectural analysis. This is a thoughtful exploration of what's technically possible.

After considering the options, I think the right approach for now is option #3: make launching from Myrlin easy enough that external sessions become rare. We've been investing in the Launcher, session discovery, and the new AI-powered session finder (v0.9.0) to make this friction-free.

For the /dev/tty and tmux approaches, the complexity and edge cases (concurrent input, platform differences, PTY ownership) outweigh the benefit for a local dev tool. That said, read-only session mirroring is an interesting idea we may revisit once the core experience is more mature.

Keeping this open as a tracked enhancement for future consideration. Appreciate the contribution!
